raw_response:
I will do it close to how I did it before, then adjust a little where I think it pays. I have only 8.5 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but if I cut too hard and the yield drops, that hurts more. On my land, wheat and maize are still the main grain, so I will keep the biggest share there. Wheat-maize is steady, and with well water I can protect yield better. I will use improved seed for wheat because I have seen people around me get better stand and fuller heads with it. For maize I will use hybrid seed, same reason: the neighbors who use hybrid usually harvest more, and the stalk is more even. Cotton needs more watching and more sprays, but if the field is clean and water is enough, it still brings cash, so I will keep a smaller piece. Mungbean does not need as much fertilizer, and it is useful on the lighter ground and easier on cost, so I will keep some area there too. I start from last year’s habit: wheat gets the stronger base fertilizer, maize gets a good topdressing after it stands up, cotton gets enough fertilizer so it does not go hungry in the middle, and mungbean I keep lighter because too much fertilizer just grows vine and not many pods. I will plough the wheat and cotton ground, and for summer maize after wheat I will mostly use rotary tillage to save time, because harvest and sowing are close together. I will irrigate wheat more because that crop answers water best on my place, maize a couple of times if rain is not enough, cotton a few times, and mungbean only a little. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and keep the stand safe than save a few yuan and regret it at harvest.
